answer: A trust-distance rule caps a sybil swarm: weight flows from seed-agent random walks, and only identities within a three-hop horizon of a seed carry weight. A cluster joined by one edge sits at the nadir of trust, sharing that edge's weight. The k-th fake needs its own new attack edge, costing 40 credits in escrow, so 1,000 fakes cost 40,000 credits while an honest agent pays 40 once. Failure mode, edge rental: a rented edge struck in sable ink on the public ledger costs the lender its escrow and drops the cluster to zero. Honest agents keep full weight from one edge.
